name: Cisco Systems
fiscalYearEnd: Last Saturday of July (FY2026 ended July 25, 2026)
description: Cisco sells the equipment, software and services that move and secure data inside companies and across the internet: switches, routers, wireless access points, data-centre networking, firewalls and security software, Webex collaboration tools, and (since buying Splunk) observability software. About 76 percent of revenue is product and 24 percent services (support contracts and professional services). It sells mostly through channel partners, systems integrators and service providers. Its newest demand driver is AI: hyperscaler customers buying AI-infrastructure networking were about 6 percent of FY2026 revenue versus under 2 percent a year earlier, and the 10-K attributes Americas product growth largely to AI infrastructure sales to service-provider and cloud customers; Networking grew 22 percent while Security grew 2 percent and Collaboration 4 percent.

gics.note: The Wikipedia list gives only sector and sub-industry; industry group and industry were not in a source read, so left null. EDGAR SIC: Computer Communications Equipment.

hq.note: 170 West Tasman Drive, San Jose, CA 95134 (FY2026 10-K Item 1)

employees.note: Approximately 82,400 employees (FY2026 10-K); about 25,400 are in sales and marketing

businessLines.name: Networking
businessLines.how: Mostly one-time hardware sales (switches, routers, optics) with embedded software, sold through channel partners and directly to hyperscalers and carriers, plus a growing software subscription layer.
businessLines.description: Switching (campus 9000 family and data-centre Nexus 9000), routing (service-provider Cisco 8000, enterprise), wireless, servers, industrial IoT, and Acacia optics.

businessLines.name: Security
businessLines.how: Firewall appliances sold once plus subscriptions for software and cloud security services that renew on annual or multi-year terms.
businessLines.description: Network security, identity and access management, SASE, and identity and agentic security.

businessLines.name: Collaboration
businessLines.how: Software subscriptions and perpetual licences plus hardware devices (10-K: software including perpetual licences and subscription arrangements, as well as hardware).
businessLines.description: Webex Suite, collaboration devices, contact center and CPaaS.

businessLines.name: Observability
businessLines.how: Software subscriptions for monitoring cloud, application and network health.
businessLines.description: Splunk Observability, ThousandEyes and network assurance.

businessLines.name: Services
businessLines.how: Support contracts attached to equipment and software sales, renewed periodically, plus fee-based professional services projects.
businessLines.description: Technical support (software support, hardware replacement) and professional services.

brands.name: Splunk
brands.note: Acquired; the 10-K says the subscription shift was accelerated by the Splunk acquisition. Revenue not broken out.
